chunks: And Ibn Abī Laylā said to al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام:
“What thing is sweeter than what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has created?” So he said: “The young child.”
He said: “What thing is more bitter than what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has created?” He said: “Losing him.”
So he said: “I bear witness that you are the proofs of Allah over His creation.”

key_terms.أَحْلَى: sweeter; the most delightful or pleasing
key_terms.أَمَرُّ: more bitter; more painful or grievous
key_terms.حُجَجُ: proofs; divinely appointed authorities and evidences
key_terms.فَقْدُهُ: losing him; the loss of that child
key_terms.ٱلشَّابُّ: young; here describing the child in youthful age
key_terms.ٱلصَّادِقِ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, addressed in this narration

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say is the sweetest and most bitter thing in human experience?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys the sweetness of having a young child and the bitterness of losing one. It also reflects recognition of the Imam's profound wisdom, leading Ibn Abī Laylā to testify that the Ahl al-Bayt are Allah’s proofs over creation.
